notes:
The whole list is on n12.jpg (printed p. 5). n10 and n11 (pp. 3–4) are the text before it, and n13 (p. 6) carries on the footnotes.

Layout: The heading is 'East Coast of Scotland.' in small capitals. Above the asterisk columns is a year header reading '79 '80 '81 '82 '83. No sentence explains the asterisks, but the text on p. 4 says 'Twelve stations on this coast have sent in forty-two schedules' for 1883. Exactly 12 rows have an asterisk under '83 (nos. 4, 7, 10, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20, 26, 27, 28), so the asterisks are clearly returns received in each year. The footnotes agree: no. 18, Tarbat Ness, and no. 17, Noss Head, are thanked for their 'first schedule' or 'first return' and have only '83. No. 25, Montroseness, sent no returns in 1882 and has no asterisks. No. 22, Kinnaird Head, sent no schedule in 1882 and has none. In 'marks' I name the year column each asterisk sits under, worked out from its position. Neither 'printed' nor 'marks' keeps a few stray specks: a tick before the 3rd asterisk in row 5, a tick between the 3rd and 4th in row 8, and a dot before the first in row 27.

No light types (L.H./L.V.) or characters are printed. The figure column is the height of the light: '230 ft.' on the first row, then ditto marks ',,'. I've put it in 'other' as printed. I've kept the full stops after keepers' names because they are printed, and footnote marks stay attached as printed (D. McDonald.†, W.Davidson.‡, J. McGill.§). For the roll of keepers, drop the trailing '.' and the footnote marks. Leader-dot runs ('......') are approximate in length. The dots in 'Land Notes.—7b.' are printed as is, and the 'b' is a small capital (7B). The sub-headings Orkney and Mainland are in small capitals. Rows 4–7 and 7b sit under the main heading only, with no sub-heading.

Copied as printed, worth flagging:
- No. 20 is printed 'Chanonry, Point Elgin', with the comma misplaced; it means Chanonry Point, Elgin (really Ross-shire). I've given name 'Chanonry' and place 'Point Elgin' as printed.
- No. 25 'Montroseness, Aberdeen': Montrose is in Forfarshire.
- No. 13 is 'Cantick Head' (the OCR's 'Caritick' is wrong).
- 'North Ronaldshay', 'Whalsey', 'Girdleness', 'Montroseness' and 'Inch Keith' are the period spellings.
- 'W.Davidson.' has no space after the initial.
- In nos. 16 and 22 the type is set tight ('HolbornHead,Caithness', 'KinnairdHead,Aberdeen'). I've normalised the spacing to 'Holborn Head, Caithness' and 'Kinnaird Head, Aberdeen'.

The image differs from the OCR in several heights: Sumburgh 300 (OCR 3800), Pentland Skerries 170 (OCR 270), Buchan Ness 130 (OCR 180), Whalsey 143 (OCR 148), Covesea 160, Hoy Sound (High) 115.

Keepers:
- D. Laidlaw is printed for both Dunnet Head (15) and Holborn Head (16). That's possibly an error in the print, since one keeper is unlikely to have served both.
- Pentland Skerries has a brace joining D. McDonald.† and J. Gilmour. The † footnote says Mr D. McDonald moved from Pentland Skerries to Skervuile (W. C.) about July 26th and sent returns until then; after that Mr J. Gilmour took over the returns. Note that Auskerry's keeper is a different McDonald (J. McDonald).
- The ‡ footnote (Tarbat Ness) thanks Mr W. Davidson for the first schedule from there.
- The p. 6 text gives no. 17's keeper in full as Mr Alexander Greig.
- D. M. Scott, at no. 7 Sumburgh Head, is 'now at Sumburgh Head'. The || footnote, on Kinnaird Head, says he left that station and moved to Sumburgh Head.
- The § footnote is on Chanonry and Mr McGill, who has been there since the summer of 1882.
- The ¶ footnote reads: '"No Birds" at Montroseness, reason given for absence of returns in 1882 (q. v.).'

Count: nos. 4–29 plus 7b make 27 entries; nos. 1–3 are not in this list. The p. 4 text says the ordinary papers went to thirty stations on the East Coast of Scotland, Faroe and Iceland, out of 'twenty-six E.C. stations of Scotland', which matches nos. 4–29.
